deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Gauss manuscript. It is the printed errata leaf ('Druckfehler') of the book bound into the bundle 'HB.Leiste'. The book ends on the previous page with the imprint 'Wolfenbüttel, aus der Bindseilschen Buchdruckerey, 1790'. It is very probably Christian Leiste's elementary textbook of arithmetic and algebra (Wolfenbüttel, 1790); the bundle name suggests this, and I cannot confirm the title from this page alone. Gauss's own handwritten notes appear only on the next page: prime-counting values such as 9593 primes below 100000, and a series inversion.

The errata entries, read as mathematics:

(1) Several entries only correct cross-references (§13→§15, §19→§18, §104→§106, §14→§15, and a missing '§.30') or wording ('heißt'→'giebt', 'Dinge'→'Nur Dinge', 'oder'→'und', 'die Produkte'→'einige Produkte', 'Fartors'→'Factors', 'so ist'→'so bekommt man').

(2) Numerical corrections:
- 243/130 → 243/120
- 1.52 → 1.512
- 149235/563000 → 194235/563000
- 1971,175 → 1971,125
- 100/10,73 → 100/1073
- c = 25000 → c = 25 or 25,000
- 5x+12 ggr. → 5x+72 ggr. (ggr. = Gute Groschen)
- (12−1) ggr. → (12−1) pf. (a unit slip, groschen versus pfennig)
- 'nach s' → 'nach 5'

(3) Algebraic corrections:
- (6ba²b³) → (6a²b³).
- §75: (a²+ab+b²) → (a²+2ab+b²). This is the binomial square (a+b)².
- p.71: n²+2n+1 → n²−2n+1, i.e. (n−1)².
- p.85: (13/12)(x−3) → (13/12)x − 3.
- p.94: ±√(f−49) → ±√(f²−4g). This is the discriminant in the quadratic formula x = (−f ± √(f²−4g))/2 for x² + fx + g = 0. My reading of the normalization is inferred, not stated on the page.
- p.44, §115: the inserted justification reads 'since for (1+x)/(1−x) = 10 one has, in the series of §113, x = 9/11, as for K in §112'. Solving (1+x)/(1−x) = 10 gives 1+x = 10−10x, so 11x = 9 and x = 9/11. This is the standard substitution in the logarithmic series ln((1+x)/(1−x)) = 2(x + x³/3 + x⁵/5 + …), used here to compute ln 10 (presumably the modulus K of §112).

Context from the previous page: the book closes by approximating a given number, evidently 1/π ≈ 0.3183098862, with continued-fraction convergents [0;3,7,15,1]. These give 106/331 and 113/355. It states that 113/355 is 'not quite 3/100000000 smaller than the given value'. The book's sign is wrong: 113/355 lies above 1/π by about 2.7·10⁻⁸ (see errors). The size of the gap is consistent with the stated bound.
errors: The printed errata themselves look mathematically sound: (1+x)/(1−x)=10 gives x=9/11; a²+2ab+b² is (a+b)²; f²−4g is the correct discriminant for x²+fx+g=0.
The errata entry for p.94 reproduces the misprint as 'f−49', presumably a typographic corruption of f²−4g. The correction itself is right.

On the previous page, the book claims 113/355 is slightly smaller than the target 1/π. In fact 113/355 = 0.31830985915… exceeds 1/π = 0.31830988618…? Checking: 0.318309859 < 0.318309886, so 113/355 is smaller, by about 2.7e-8. The book is correct after all; no error.

results.what: Printed errata list of a 1790 Wolfenbüttel arithmetic/algebra textbook (probably Leiste); not Gauss's work
results.modern_name: Errata sheet (binomial square, quadratic discriminant, logarithmic series substitution)

results.what: Using (1+x)/(1−x)=10, i.e. x=9/11, in the series ln((1+x)/(1−x)) = 2Σx^(2k+1)/(2k+1) to compute ln 10
results.modern_name: Gregory/Euler logarithmic series for computing logarithms
results.usually_credited_to: James Gregory / Edmond Halley / Euler (17th–18th c.)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed errata list of someone else's 1790 textbook bound into the bundle, with no Gauss handwriting or original mathematics.

checkable.asserts: The corrected expression n²−2n+1 is (n−1)² (errata p.71)
The discriminant f²−4g in the quadratic formula (errata p.94)
About 2.7e-8 (positive), i.e. 113/355 is smaller than 1/pi by less than 3e-8 (previous page)

transcription_corrections: 'rc.' in the entries for p.51 and p.86 is the Fraktur abbreviation 'ꝛc.' (= etc.), not the letters 'rc'.
Entry for p.94: the image shows the misprinted form '±√(f—49' with the closing parenthesis missing, as quoted in the 'statt' part; the transcription's '(f−49)' adds a parenthesis.
Entry for p.86: the 'statt' reading in the image is '5x÷12 ggr.' (plus sign badly printed), corrected to '5x+72 ggr.'.
